newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore oil products steady despite stocks hike.
newsitem.headline: Singapore oil products steady despite stocks hike.

text.p: Singapore oil products were steady to marginally lower on Thursday despite the across-the-barrel rise in Singapore weekly stocks data issued by the Trade Development Board, traders said.

Gas oil stocks rose to its highest level in 10 months to hit 8.42 million barrels. But gas oil swaps, which dipped 30 cents a barrel from Wednesday even before the data was known, did not plunge after its release, on support from a firm London gas oil market, brokers said. October swaps traded between $27.90 and $28. Traders said there were still no signs the rally in Europe would abate despite cargoes from the US Gulf Coast placed there.

Physical gas oil was earlier offered lower to $27.85 for Oct 16-20 lifting fob, 10-15 cents below Wednesday. But the offer was withdrawn when met with a bid. Traders said India agreed to take 180,000 tonnes more diesel under its renewed annual term deal with Kuwait, bringing the volume for the 1996-1997 contract to 1.68 million tonnes.

The recent jet fuel maximisation has resulted in abundant supplies but limited outlets. Indonesia seemed to be the only buyer having bought prompt cargoes around 10-15 cents premium to Singapore quotes fob. Jet fuel was offered lower for Oct 11-15 lifting at $29.50, with a bid for an earlier date at $29.45.
This was under the deal done Wednesday at $29.70 for Oct 20-24 lifting between a Singapore and a Mediterranean traders.

Naphtha inched up on firmer swap values and rises in overnight crude prices. October paper was quoted at $21.30/21.55, up from Wednesday's close of $21.15/21.30. Gasoline was unchanged in thin trading. Traders said the market was balanced with sales seen from Thailand for 92-octane at premiums of 10 cents fob Rayong and 90 cents cost-and-freight Singapore. In Singapore, a buyer was seen for a 95 octane cargo loading Oct 19-23 at 22.80 fob. Fuel oil was stable with discussions around $115-118. --Singapore Newsroom (+65-870 3084)
